summary.tldr: Changes bail and release rules for some violent offences, adds stricter detention rules in repeat cases, and requires an annual report on judicial interim release.
what_it_does: Replaces the main release principle with public protection, and tells police, justices and judges to give public safety primary weight when deciding release.
Adds more violent offences to reverse-onus bail rules, creates a new category of “major offence”, and blocks police from releasing someone arrested for a major offence.

Requires a superior court judge to decide release in some repeat major-offence cases, and orders detention if the person was already on release for another major offence and had a major offence conviction in the past 10 years.
Ends interim release when a person is convicted of an indictable offence while awaiting sentence, and bars people convicted of an indictable offence in the past 10 years from acting as a surety.

Requires release decisions to consider whether the accused is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and, if not, whether they may leave Canada, and makes passport surrender mandatory for some non-resident accused.

Requires the Minister of Justice to table a yearly report on judicial interim release, including release outcomes, compliance, recidivism, public-attention incidents, effectiveness of conditions, and disparities between groups.
summary.background: The bill amends the Criminal Code rules on judicial interim release and the Department of Justice Act. It adds a yearly reporting duty on the state of judicial interim release in Canada.
